name: Temporal Equivalence Principle: Temporal Horizon Cosmology and the Absence of a Physical Big Bang Singularity
description: Standard FLRW cosmology extrapolates observed cosmic expansion backward to $a(t)\to0$, producing a Big Bang singularity at finite proper time. This paper demonstrates that this singularity is a reconstruction artifact of imposing a globally isochronous expanding-frame description on a conformal temporal geometry. In the Temporal Equivalence Principle (TEP), the observational role of FLRW expansion is reconstructed through conformal temporal transport: the effective scale factor $a_{\rm eff}$ arises from accumulated open-path conformal temporal shear along cosmological lines of sight rather than from physical expansion of space. TEP-C0 (Paper 26) established the distance-redshift and supernova evidence ; the conditional nonsingular matter-frame boundary construction is developed here. Realization of that boundary within the complete infinite inhomogeneous solution remains the common-action construction problem of Paper 0.
